review.tagline: Python library that lets an LLM agent control a web browser
review.summary: Browser Use runs an LLM-driven agent that opens a browser, reads pages and completes tasks such as searching, filling forms and booking slots. It is used as a Python library (3.11+), as a CLI skill for agents like Claude Code, or through a hosted cloud API. It works with OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Ollama and its own BU2 model, on local or cloud browsers.
review.audience: Developers building browser-automating agents in Python
strengths: Works with a local Chrome profile, a cloud browser, or a remote browser over CDP
Custom tools register with a decorator; system prompt can be extended or overridden
Supports OpenAI, Anthropic and Google wrappers, plus local models via Ollama
Ships a CLI skill so existing coding agents can drive a browser
weaknesses: README recommends BU2, which needs a paid Browser Use API key
CAPTCHA and stealth handling rely on the paid cloud browser, with no guarantee
Profile sync copies cookies only, not local storage, IndexedDB or extensions
Hardware needs for local models are not stated in the README
needs: Needs Python >= 3.11, Chromium-based browser, LLM provider API key or Ollama, Browser Use API key (optional)
Models: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Ollama, BU2 (ChatBrowserUse)
